payloads.author: erickdavestech
payloads.release_notes:
On-screen **DualSense controller overlay** for a PS5 running homebrew. Load it once per boot, open any game, and the controller appears bottom-left, lighting up in real time.

## Download

`ps5-dualsense-overlay-v1.0.1.elf` — SHA-256 in `SHA256SUMS.txt`:

```text
3790c590088b275a8d803c7c46394af6c7e0d8ede2546c0507a05a246fbf9747  ps5-dualsense-overlay-v1.0.1.elf
```

## What's Changed in v1.0.1

### Fixed
- **Overlay freeze after Rest Mode (sleep/resume):** Fixed issue where `sceUserServiceGetForegroundUser` returning `0xffffffff` (-1) during console standby or before logging into an account caused pad initialization to permanently fail, leaving the overlay visible on screen but completely frozen.
- **Controller disconnect / standby recovery:** If `scePadReadState` fails continuously for 15 consecutive frames (e.g. controller turned off, Bluetooth drop, or system suspend), the dead handle is now safely closed via `scePadClose` and re-acquired automatically as soon as the controller is back online.

### Added
- **Periodic foreground user detection:** The overlay now checks for foreground user account switches every ~2 seconds and re-binds the pad handle when switching local accounts.
- **Non-blocking pad initialization retry:** Periodic retry every 30 frames (~0.5s) if user or handle was not immediately ready at startup.

## Usage

1. Jailbreak the console as usual (tested with kstuff-lite).
2. Load `ps5-dualsense-overlay-v1.0.1.elf` with your payload manager, in either of these ways:
   - **Web portal:** from a PC or phone on the same network, open the payload manager's portal using the console's local IP and upload the `.elf`.
   - **USB:** copy the `.elf` to a USB drive, connect it to the console and launch it from the payload manager.
3. Open any game.

Load it only **once** per boot, and do not run it together with Common FPS or SimpleFPS: they inject into the same system process. To update, reboot and load the new version.

payloads.name: hush
payloads.author: disco-trooper
payloads.release_notes:
## A leftover `state.txt` no longer looks like a live patch

`/data/hush/state.txt` exists while the patch is in place and is deleted once
every slot is restored. Tools read it that way: PS5Upload's upcoming hold-mode
support ([phantomptr/ps5upload#651](https://github.com/phantomptr/ps5upload/issues/651))
waits for the file to go before starting a stream.

A reboot drops the patch but not the file. After a boot with `hold_s=0`, a
console switched to hold mode kept the old `state.txt` until the first game's
window ended. Until then every stream would wait and pause for nothing.

In hold mode Hush now checks on start, and on `enabled=0`, whether any slot is
redirected. If none is, it deletes the leftover file and logs:

```
removed a stale /data/hush/state.txt: no slot is redirected
```

Checked on 13.60 with a planted `state.txt` from an earlier boot: removed at start.

Nothing else changed. With `hold_s=0` the next start patches again and rewrites
the file, as before.

### Install

```
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS      # Linux
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS  # macOS
```

Replace `hush.elf` in Payload Manager. Existing `config.ini` files keep working.

### Build

```
e58045cc39bb2301a4966e3c043eb75cabc45a0e5e39bb09b0b4151f57767f78  hush.elf
```

Reproducible with the same toolchain (`-Wl,--build-id=none`): two clean builds of
this tag gave this exact binary. Built with Homebrew clang/LLD 23.1.4.

payloads.name: librespot-ps5
payloads.author: stupiditytries
payloads.release_notes:
First release. Spotify Connect on a modified PS5, playing over your games.

## What you need

- A PS5 that can load ELF payloads
- [klogsrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/klogsrv) running on the console
- A USB drive the console plays music from (exFAT or FAT32, not extended storage) with about 8 GB free
- Spotify Premium, and the Spotify app on a phone on the same network as the console

## How to use it

1. Download `librespot-ps5.elf` below, put it on a USB drive and load it with your payload loader.
2. On the console, open the **Music** tab in the control centre.
3. Go to your **external drive**.
4. Open the folder **Start Librespot** and play **Librespot Streamer**.
5. In the Spotify app on your phone, open the device list and pick **PS5 Connect**.

The program makes the folders and tracks itself the first time it runs. If they do not show up in the music list, open any other music folder once and go back.

After you press play on the console there are about 14 seconds of silence before the music starts. After that, everything you do in the Spotify app is heard about two seconds later, and the music keeps playing when you start a game.

To stop, play **Stop Librespot** in the folder **Librespot Controls**, or pause from the phone.

## Known issues

- Track notifications show on the home screen but not yet while a game is in front.
- Pausing from the console costs about 14 seconds of silence when you resume. Pausing from the phone does not.
- Next and Previous on the console do nothing useful; use the phone.
- After 12 hours the stream has to be started again.
- Tested on one console and one USB drive.

How it works, the settings and the build steps are in the [README](https://github.com/stupiditytries/librespot-ps5#readme).

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Spotify or Sony.

payloads.name: pegasus-dl

payloads.release_notes:
- Parallel downloads now use persistent connections and write ranges directly
  into the temporary file, avoiding a final segment-copy pass. New configurations
  default to 16 connections, with a single-stream fallback for incompatible hosts.
- RAR/RAR5 and 7z archive cache downloads use the same parallel engine. Paused
  downloads resume from checked checkpoints, and paused extraction restarts from
  the completed cache without downloading again.
- Completed RAR caches survive password prompts and wrong passwords. UTF-8
  passwords and retries for legacy encrypted RAR files are handled correctly.
- Extraction progress now counts bytes across files. Cancellation and
  finalization are coordinated to avoid committing cancelled work.
- Archive replacement failures restore the previous destination, stored RAR
  entries receive CRC checks, and failed format probes clean up their temporary
  files.

payloads.description: PS5 App Dumper 2.00 Beta PS5 App Dumper 2.10 Beta [Pre-release] by EchoStretch
payloads.author: EchoStretch
payloads.release_notes:
## Highlights

**DLC**
- Each title shows how many DLC are installed for it, with names and sizes
- Dump DLC on the running game dumps its DLC alone, next to a dump you made before, without copying the game again
- With several DLC you pick which ones; a picked DLC that is there already is replaced
- DLC dumps now carry their metadata (param.json, icon) from the installed package (#29)
- DLC that only unlock content in the game are never mounted by the console and have nothing to dump; the page says so instead of hiding the button

**Titles and dumps**
- A DUMPED badge on every title that is dumped somewhere, UNFINISHED for one that was cut short
- New dump folders carry the app title: `PPSA01325-app0_ASTRO's_PLAYROOM` (setting `folder_titles`, on by default)
- Rename on the Dumps page switches every dump to names with or without the title
- Tap a dump's path to copy it, and the Dumps list fits a phone

**Queue**
- Up to 64 titles instead of 16

**Fixes**
- Titles stuck at 99 %  were held as installing for good and could not be dumped
- The UNFINISHED badge was drawn far too big

## Notes
- Dumps made with 2.00 or earlier keep their names and are still recognised. Use Rename on the Dumps page if you want the titles on them too.
- A dump ShadowMount runs a game from is not renamed, because the link points at its folder.

## Thanks
Thanks to @MangoScango for #29, which completes the DLC dumps with their metadata.

## For developers
Built on [webhb](https://github.com/slopmaster33/webhb) 0.4.1. If its download does not work, `webhb-0.4.1.tar.gz` is attached; build with `WEBHB_TARBALL=webhb-0.4.1.tar.gz make`.

### Direct Install
- PKG files can now be installed from another device, such as a PC, directly to the console without a temporary disk copy

- PS4 and PS5 package badges are now shown in package lists

payloads.name: spotless [Pre-release]
payloads.author: abhi245y
payloads.release_notes:
First public beta of Spotless: the native Spotify app on a jailbroken PS5, signed in with your Spotify account, no PSN required.

### What works
- Sign-in with the on-screen code or Spotify Connect from your phone
- Home, browsing, songs, videos and the rest of the native app
- Background playback while gaming
- Pause, previous and next from the Now Playing card
- One-time setup that persists across launches and reboots
- `Spotless-Restore.elf` puts the original app back

### Tested
Firmware 13.00 with Spotify 01.017.000 (PPSA05688). Other firmware versions are untested; reports welcome. Spotless refuses frontend versions it does not recognise.

### Install
1. Install Spotify 01.017.000 ([package guide](https://github.com/abhi245y/spotless/blob/main/docs/PACKAGES.md)).
2. Load `Spotless.elf` with your ELF loader or Payload Manager.
3. Open Spotify and wait on the login screen for *UI patch installed*.
4. Close Spotify fully, reopen and sign in.

Full guide: [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/abhi245y/spotless/blob/main/INSTALL.md)

### Known issues
- **Music > Music sources > Spotify** still shows *Link* and opens Sony's account-linking flow. Spotify itself is signed in and works normally.

### Assets
- `Spotless.elf`, `Spotless-Restore.elf` and their `.sha256` files
- `Spotless.meta.json` for loaders that read metadata
- `merge_pkg.py` and `cleanup_console.py` (optional tools, see the docs)
- `SHA256SUMS` covering every file

payloads.name: ytps5-sponsorblock [Pre-release]
payloads.description: v1.2.0-beta.2 — firmware-agnostic test build (1.00–13.60) [Pre-release] by MasterShivnath007
payloads.author: MasterShivnath007
payloads.release_notes:
**Experimental firmware-agnostic build — testers wanted.**

This is the first build that is not tied to one firmware. Kernel addresses
are resolved at runtime from the PS5 payload SDK, so the same ELF follows
firmware **1.00 through 13.60** instead of a hard-coded table.

## What changed

- `allproc` and `root_vnode` now come from the SDK's runtime
  `KERNEL_ADDRESS_*` values; proc fields use `KERNEL_OFFSET_PROC_P_*`.
- Process walks are bounded, and the pid is re-read through the struct. An
  unknown firmware now stops with a notification instead of walking a bad
  pointer and hanging.
- 12.x and 13.x added to the fallback table: 1.00 to 13.60 is now complete
  (67 versions checked).
- Memory writes are chunked into 4 KB, retried after `mprotect`, and then
  tried through `kernel_proc_copyin`, with one `write[...]` log line per
  region that includes the protection, error number and verification.
- If a pre-hook write fails, the app is resumed instead of staying frozen.

## Verified

Firmware **8.20**, YouTube `01.000.003` (`PPSA01652`): attach, target
scan, all six writes, hook installed, **1 script injected**.

## Still unverified

- **Firmware 11.40:** this build targets the `write failed` reported in
  issue #1. It should now either succeed or name the exact failing region in
  `injector.log`. Not confirmed yet.
- **12.x / 13.x:** the kernel addresses are covered by the SDK, but the
  YouTube app build on those firmwares may use a different
  `HTMLScriptExecute` signature. If so, it stops safely at
  `target not found`.

## If you test it

Run `ytps5.elf` as usual. If it fails, send
`/data/ytps5-sponsorblock/injector.log`. The log now contains
`build: fw-agnostic diag`, `sdk: fw=`, `sections:`, and one
`write[...]` line per region.

SHA-256 of `ytps5.elf`: `5a63a26262cbc91782cc463679596c100cf8b4d0293624a68643c3745484f594`
